summary.title: Go CLI tutorial: fortune clone
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a basic fortune-style random quote CLI in Go by locating the fortunes directory via `fortune -f`, walking it with filepath.Walk, and splitting quote files on %.
takeaways: Ask the system `fortune -f` for the fortunes directory path, reading it from stderr via StderrPipe.
Use filepath.Walk to collect fortune files recursively while skipping .dat binaries and the /off/ offensive folder.
Pick a random quote by splitting a file's contents on lines containing % and choosing one with math/rand.
Since Go 1.20 math/rand seeds itself, so no rand.Seed call is needed.
summary.summary: The article builds a simplified clone of the Unix fortune command in Go, as the last part of a series alongside gocowsay and gololcat. It shells out to `fortune -f` to find the fortunes directory, reading the first line of stderr with a bufio scanner and trimming it to a path. It then walks the tree with filepath.Walk, skipping .dat files, directories, and the /off/ folder, and collects file names. Finally it picks a random file and a random quote separated by % lines, progressively refactoring the code into a final version. The author notes the approach is not efficient and misses many features of the original.
